memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers, put fire in them and added incense; and they offered unauthorised fire before the LORD, contrary to his command." - Lev 10:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Yesterday God's fire fell and the nation shouted for joy. Today two priests bring fire of their own, and everything changes.

We must be honest: Scripture does not tell us exactly what they did wrong. The text says only that it was unauthorised — literally, strange fire — and contrary to his command. Some suggest they took coals from an ordinary source rather than the altar. Some connect it to the warning about alcohol that follows in verse 9. We cannot be certain, and it is wiser to admit that than to invent a reason.

What the text does emphasise is the phrase repeated throughout chapters 8 and 9 — as the LORD commanded — and its sudden reversal here: contrary to his command.

These were not pagans. They were ordained priests, sons of Aaron, men who had stood at the altar the day before. Their sin was not unbelief. It was presumption: deciding that their way of approaching God was near enough.

There is a warning here worth receiving gently but seriously. God is not a formality. Nearness to holy things is not the same as reverence for them.

The safest posture before God has always been to do what He said, not what seemed reasonable to us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I ever approach God on my own terms rather than His?
2. Has familiarity with spiritual things made me casual where I should be reverent?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy, and I do not want to treat You lightly. Teach me to come to You Your way, with reverence and trust. Amen.
